A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diffusion2 and contain readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends after its references; v3 additionally contains Appendix A.1–A.5. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation examples, a user study, quantitative video-to-4D comparisons and schedule ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds text-to-4D examples and a partial-observation reconstruction evaluation in Appendix A.5, Figures 6–7 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The core SVD/SV3D score-composition and Gaussian-reconstruction framework remains. v3 adds an explicit text-to-image-to-4D input procedure with background removal and recentering (A.5). A.4 also documents two-pass initialization and view-dependent mixing, but does not establish whether these refinements were already used for v1's retained experiments.

E1.justification: v3 adds partial-observation reconstruction using both a front-view video and reference-frame multiview images from six animated models, introducing a distinct conditioning scenario and data population. Figure 6 also demonstrates explicit text-to-4D prompts. The Animate124, Consistent4D and Objaverse sources newly identified for the original experiments are provenance disclosures, not established dataset replacements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 is unchanged. For the new partial-reconstruction comparison, A.5 adapts Consistent4D by adding reference-view pixelwise reconstruction loss and rendering inputs with Zero-1-to-3 camera intrinsics. This changes the evaluated comparator variant without introducing a new baseline family.

E3.justification: A.5 introduces a ground-truth reconstruction protocol with joint conditioning observations and PSNR/SSIM evaluation on six animated models. Figure 5 also revises the reported extreme controls from pure SVD/SV3D to logistic schedules with s0=0 or 1 and k=20. This establishes changed reported settings, not that the retained ablations were rerun.

E4.justification: The original schedule-sensitivity analysis remains, with its extreme settings recharacterized as model-dominant mixtures. A.4 adds an unquantified experimental finding that two-pass initialization reduces failures more effectively than simply doubling inference steps. No dedicated numerical ablation accompanies this additional comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3's participant count describes the existing user study; its two sampling passes are algorithmic steps, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All scores, preference percentages and generation times in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. New Table 3 reports PSNR/SSIM of 18.41/0.87 for Consistent4D, 20.45/0.89 for Diffusion2-stage1 and 21.55/0.90 for stage2. Figures 6–7 add text-conditioned and reconstruction results. These extend the evidence to new settings rather than establish same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1 changes from independence between entire row/column sets to a pairwise-image formulation. New A.3 supplies a rotation counterexample, continuity and local-independence assumptions, and an approximate derivation of the score decomposition. This substantially expands and revises the theoretical conditions, although the main theorem's displayed conclusion remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: zero-shot composition of video and multiview priors, parallel generation without 4D training data, efficient reconstruction and flexible conditioning. The additional experiments and qualifications do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: A.2–A.3 explicitly discuss textureless backs, corrupted motion and rotations that violate the independence assumption, extending v1's limited caveats. A.4 explains domain and viewpoint biases; A.5 explains choosing image-mediated text generation and attributes reconstruction-score advantages partly to camera alignment. These materially qualify applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies eight A6000 GPUs, a 33.8-degree field of view, a 2 m camera radius, dataset provenance, four-view CLIP averaging, and 50 user-study participants evaluating eight named samples. A.4 adds initialization and view-weighting formulas, including a 25-step preliminary pass. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly credits MultiDiffusion and SyncDiffusion as inspiration and adds references for FreeInit, variational autoencoders and additional Gaussian representations. It removes the HexPlane and Sora-geometrical-consistency references. The broad positioning against SDS-based generation and Efficient4D remains.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewriting extends across the introduction, related work, method and experiments. Separate task-result subsections become one Main results section; conditioning and parallelism explanations are reorganized, and ablation discussion gains parameter-specific headings. These narrative revisions extend beyond simply appending new scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, Figure 3 rearranges stage rows and method labels, and Figure 5 gains revised labels and separate parameter panels. Existing tables are restyled and relocated, while Figures 6–7 and Table 3 add new displays. The changes substantially affect visual presentation, despite retaining many original examples.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves auditability by supplying study, dataset and hardware details missing from v1, whose user-study appendix reference had no accompanying appendix. It adds ground-truth fidelity evaluation beyond CLIP similarity and explicitly identifies failures of the central assumption. These address important documentation and applicability gaps. A.3 remains an approximate argument and statistical uncertainty remains unreported, so the improvement does not establish fully resolved theoretical or statistical rigor.
